panels.description:
One row per merged pull request in the selected project(s) and time range, by merge date, newest first. Use it to trace bug-fix PRs back to the PRs that caused them and to compare AI-assisted with non-AI PRs. The PR column shows every number with `#`, including GitLab MRs, which GitLab writes as `!123`.

- **Ticket** is the first of these that the PR has:
  1. Issue keys such as Jira's in `pull_request_issues`, written by the linker plugin.
  2. A Jira-style key (`ABC-123`) in the title, then in the branch, where the branch may use lower case. Its prefix must appear as a key in at least 3 PRs of the selected projects' repositories, so one-off terms such as `AES-256` are skipped. Technical terms such as `UTF-8`, `SHA-256`, `CVE-2024` and `HTTP-2` are always skipped.
  3. GitHub's linked issue numbers in `pull_request_issues`, which GitHub reads from words such as `closes #123` in the PR body.
  4. `#123` in the title or branch. Colours such as `#1890ff`, another repository's `org/repo#456`, and PR references such as `(#123)`, `pull request #123`, `Revert #123`, `Backport #123` and `Follow-up to #123` are ignored.
  5. A 4+ digit number between `/`, `_` or `-` in the branch name that isn't a year, a date, a revert or backport PR number, or part of a number range.
- **Approvers** are reviewers whose latest approve, request-changes or dismissed review is an approval, so an approval that was later withdrawn or dismissed isn't listed. GitHub reviews and GitLab approvals are recorded. Bitbucket and Bitbucket Server don't record reviews, so they show *n/a*. For GitHub, the GraphQL collector reads at most 100 reviews per PR. Deleted accounts show as *Unknown user*.
- **Files Changed** counts distinct file paths across the PR's single-parent commits, which include a squash or rebase merge result, so a file changed and then reverted inside the PR still counts. A two-parent merge commit is skipped. It needs commit file data from the git extractor, which is collected only when `SKIP_COMMIT_FILES=false`. The default is `true`, and prod and staging keep it, so there this column shows *n/a*. It fills in only if the setting is turned off and the repositories are collected again in full refresh mode. Otherwise it shows *n/a* when none of the PR's commits have it. For rebase-merged PRs whose branch was deleted, only the last rebased commit is in the clone, so the count is low.
- **Claude Co-Authored** is Yes when any commit in the PR, or its merge commit, has a `Co-Authored-By:` line with `noreply@anthropic.com`. Commit messages come from the cloned repository and, for GitHub, from the PR commits the GitHub plugin collects, so squash- and rebase-merged PRs are still checked after their branch is deleted. For GitHub, the GraphQL collector reads only the first 100 commits of a PR. *Unknown* means no commit message was found for the PR. A two-parent merge commit without that line doesn't count, so a GitLab MR whose only stored commit is its merge commit is *Unknown*. Release and back-merge PRs carry every commit they promote, so they are Yes when any of those commits are.

targets.rawSql:
WITH prs AS (
  SELECT pr.id, pr.base_repo_id, pr.pull_request_key, pr.url, pr.title, pr.head_ref, pr.author_id, pr.author_name, pr.merged_date, pr.merge_commit_sha
  FROM pull_requests pr
  WHERE pr.base_repo_id IN (SELECT pm.row_id FROM project_mapping pm WHERE pm.`table` = 'repos' AND pm.project_name IN (SELECT upm_g.project_name FROM user_project_mapping upm_g WHERE upm_g.user_login = ${__user.login:sqlstring} AND upm_g.project_name IN ($project)))
    AND ('__all' IN ($repo_id) OR pr.base_repo_id IN ($repo_id))
    AND pr.status = 'MERGED' AND $__timeFilter(pr.merged_date)
    AND ('__all' IN ($developer) OR (pr.author_id LIKE 'github:GithubAccount:%' AND CONCAT('gh:', SUBSTRING_INDEX(pr.author_id, ':', -1)) IN ($developer)))
),
linked AS (
  -- Issue keys such as Jira's come from the linker plugin; plain numbers are GitHub's links, which
  -- it reads loosely from the PR body, so they come after a key from the title or branch below.
  SELECT pri.pull_request_id,
    GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT IF(pri.issue_key REGEXP '^[0-9]+$', NULL, pri.issue_key) ORDER BY pri.issue_key SEPARATOR ', ') AS issue_keys,
    GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT IF(pri.issue_key REGEXP '^[0-9]+$', CONCAT('#', pri.issue_key), NULL) ORDER BY pri.issue_key SEPARATOR ', ') AS numbers
  FROM pull_request_issues pri
  WHERE pri.pull_request_id IN (SELECT id FROM prs) AND pri.issue_key <> ''
  GROUP BY pri.pull_request_id
),
project_repos AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT pm.row_id AS repo_id FROM project_mapping pm WHERE pm.`table` = 'repos' AND pm.project_name IN (SELECT upm_g.project_name FROM user_project_mapping upm_g WHERE upm_g.user_login = ${__user.login:sqlstring} AND upm_g.project_name IN ($project))
),
known_prefixes AS (
  -- Prefixes used as an upper-case key in the title or branch of at least 3 PRs in the selected
  -- projects' repositories. All their PRs count, not only the filtered ones, so a PR's Ticket doesn't
  -- change with the Repository, Developer or time filters. A per-repository count missed real keys
  -- whose PRs are spread over many repositories.
  SELECT SUBSTRING_INDEX(k.issue_key, '-', 1) AS prefix
  FROM (
    SELECT p.id, REGEXP_SUBSTR(p.title, '(?<![[:alnum:]])(?!(?:UTF|SHA|CVE|HTTP|TLS|SSL|ISO|RFC|PEP|IPV|DNS|SPRINT|GPT|RELEASE|HOTFIX|STAGING|AUTO|PERF|PVT|VERSION)-)[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]{1,6}(?![0-9])', 1, 1, 'c') AS issue_key
    FROM project_repos r JOIN pull_requests p ON p.base_repo_id = r.repo_id
    UNION ALL
    SELECT p.id, REGEXP_SUBSTR(p.head_ref, '(?<![[:alnum:]])(?!(?:UTF|SHA|CVE|HTTP|TLS|SSL|ISO|RFC|PEP|IPV|DNS|SPRINT|GPT|RELEASE|HOTFIX|STAGING|AUTO|PERF|PVT|VERSION)-)[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]{1,6}(?![0-9])', 1, 1, 'c')
    FROM project_repos r JOIN pull_requests p ON p.base_repo_id = r.repo_id
  ) k
  WHERE k.issue_key IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY prefix
  HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT k.id) >= 3
),
title_keys AS (
  -- The first key in the title (upper case only), then in the branch (any case), whose prefix is
  -- known. This skips one-off terms such as AES-256.
  SELECT t.id, t.issue_key
  FROM (
    SELECT c.id, c.issue_key, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.id ORDER BY c.pos) AS rn
    FROM (
      SELECT prs.id, n.n AS pos, REGEXP_SUBSTR(prs.title, '(?<![[:alnum:]])(?!(?:UTF|SHA|CVE|HTTP|TLS|SSL|ISO|RFC|PEP|IPV|DNS|SPRINT|GPT|RELEASE|HOTFIX|STAGING|AUTO|PERF|PVT|VERSION)-)[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]{1,6}(?![0-9])', 1, n.n, 'c') AS issue_key
      FROM prs CROSS JOIN (SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3) n
      UNION ALL
      SELECT prs.id, 3 + n.n, UPPER(REGEXP_SUBSTR(prs.head_ref, '(?<![[:alnum:]])(?!(?:UTF|SHA|CVE|HTTP|TLS|SSL|ISO|RFC|PEP|IPV|DNS|SPRINT|GPT|RELEASE|HOTFIX|STAGING|AUTO|PERF|PVT|VERSION)-)[A-Z][A-Z0-9]+-[0-9]{1,6}(?![0-9])', 1, n.n, 'i'))
      FROM prs CROSS JOIN (SELECT 1 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3) n
    ) c
    JOIN known_prefixes kp ON kp.prefix = SUBSTRING_INDEX(c.issue_key, '-', 1)
  ) t
  WHERE t.rn = 1
),
pr_commits AS (
  SELECT prc.pull_request_id, prc.commit_sha FROM pull_request_commits prc WHERE prc.pull_request_id IN (SELECT id FROM prs)
  UNION
  SELECT id, merge_commit_sha FROM prs WHERE merge_commit_sha <> ''
),
merge_commits AS (
  -- The PRs' two-parent merge commits, found once for claude and file_commits.
  SELECT cp.commit_sha FROM commit_parents cp
  WHERE cp.commit_sha IN (SELECT commit_sha FROM pr_commits)
  GROUP BY cp.commit_sha HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
),
claude AS (
  SELECT m.pull_request_id, SUM(m.claude) AS commits
  FROM (
    SELECT pc.pull_request_id, CONVERT(c.message USING utf8mb4) LIKE '%noreply@anthropic.com%' AND REGEXP_LIKE(CONVERT(c.message USING utf8mb4), 'co-authored-by:[^\\n\\\\]*noreply@anthropic[.]com', 'i') AS claude,
      pc.commit_sha IN (SELECT commit_sha FROM merge_commits) AS is_merge
    FROM pr_commits pc JOIN commits c ON c.sha = pc.commit_sha
    UNION ALL
    -- The column is utf8mb4_bin, so it is converted for the LIKE to ignore case, as above.
    SELECT pc.pull_request_id, CONVERT(gc.message USING utf8mb4) LIKE '%noreply@anthropic.com%' AND REGEXP_LIKE(CONVERT(gc.message USING utf8mb4), 'co-authored-by:[^\\n\\\\]*noreply@anthropic[.]com', 'i'), 0
    FROM pr_commits pc JOIN _tool_github_commits gc ON gc.sha = pc.commit_sha
  ) m
  -- A two-parent merge commit counts only when it has the trailer. Its "Merge branch" message isn't
  -- evidence for No, so a GitLab MR whose only stored commit is its merge commit stays Unknown.
  WHERE m.claude OR NOT m.is_merge
  GROUP BY m.pull_request_id
),
file_commits AS (
  SELECT pc.pull_request_id, pc.commit_sha
  FROM pr_commits pc
  WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM commit_files cf WHERE cf.commit_sha = pc.commit_sha)
    AND pc.commit_sha NOT IN (SELECT commit_sha FROM merge_commits)
),
files AS (
  SELECT fc.pull_request_id, COUNT(DISTINCT cf.file_path) AS files
  FROM file_commits fc JOIN commit_files cf ON cf.commit_sha = fc.commit_sha
  GROUP BY fc.pull_request_id
),
latest_reviews AS (
  SELECT c.pull_request_id, c.account_id, c.status,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.pull_request_id, c.account_id ORDER BY c.created_date DESC, c.id DESC) AS rn
  FROM pull_request_comments c
  WHERE c.status IN ('APPROVED', 'CHANGES_REQUESTED', 'DISMISSED') AND c.pull_request_id IN (SELECT id FROM prs)
),
approvers AS (
  SELECT lr.pull_request_id, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT COALESCE(NULLIF(a.full_name, ''), NULLIF(a.user_name, ''), 'Unknown user') ORDER BY 1 SEPARATOR ', ') AS names
  FROM latest_reviews lr LEFT JOIN accounts a ON a.id = lr.account_id
  WHERE lr.rn = 1 AND lr.status = 'APPROVED'
  GROUP BY lr.pull_request_id
)
-- The default 256KB join buffer makes the joins below spill to disk over long ranges.
SELECT /*+ SET_VAR(join_buffer_size=67108864) */
  r.name AS "Repository",
  prs.pull_request_key AS "PR",
  prs.url AS "url",
  prs.title AS "Title",
  prs.head_ref AS "Branch",
  COALESCE(
    li.issue_keys,
    tk.issue_key,
    li.numbers,
    -- #123 in the title or branch, not inside a word, a colour such as #1890ff, another repository's
    -- org/repo#456, or a PR reference such as (#123) or Revert #123.
    REGEXP_SUBSTR(CONCAT_WS(' ', prs.title, prs.head_ref), '(?<![[:alnum:]/&(])(?<!request |revert |reverts |backport |backport of |follow-up to |follow up to |followup to |cherry-pick of |cherry pick of )#[0-9]+(?![[:alnum:]])', 1, 1, 'i'),
    -- A 4+ digit number between /, _ or - in the branch that isn't a year, a date, a revert or
    -- backport PR number, or part of a number range.
    CONCAT('#', REGEXP_SUBSTR(prs.head_ref, '(?<![^/_-])(?<![0-9]-)(?<!revert-)(?<!backport-)(?<!pr-)(?!(?:19|20)[0-9]{2}(?![0-9]))(?!(?:19|20)[0-9]{2}(?:0[1-9]|1[0-2])(?:0[1-9]|[12][0-9]|3[01])(?![0-9]))[0-9]{4,}(?![^/_-]|-[0-9])', 1, 1, 'i'))
  ) AS "Ticket",
  COALESCE(NULLIF(au.full_name, ''), prs.author_name) AS "Author",
  prs.merged_date AS "Merged",
  -- Bitbucket and Bitbucket Server don't record reviews.
  IF(prs.base_repo_id LIKE 'bitbucket%', 'n/a', ap.names) AS "Approvers",
  f.files AS "Files Changed",
  CASE WHEN cl.pull_request_id IS NULL THEN 'Unknown' WHEN cl.commits > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS "Claude Co-Authored"
FROM prs
LEFT JOIN repos r ON r.id = prs.base_repo_id
LEFT JOIN accounts au ON au.id = prs.author_id
LEFT JOIN linked li ON li.pull_request_id = prs.id
LEFT JOIN title_keys tk ON tk.id = prs.id
LEFT JOIN approvers ap ON ap.pull_request_id = prs.id
LEFT JOIN files f ON f.pull_request_id = prs.id
LEFT JOIN claude cl ON cl.pull_request_id = prs.id
ORDER BY prs.merged_date DESC

list.definition:
SELECT DISTINCT p.name AS __text, p.name AS __value
FROM projects p
INNER JOIN _tool_claude_code_otel_connection_projects cp ON cp.project_name = p.name
INNER JOIN _tool_claude_code_otel_connections c ON c.id = cp.connection_id
INNER JOIN user_project_mapping upm ON upm.project_name = p.name
WHERE c.status = 'active'
  AND upm.user_login = ${__user.login:sqlstring}
ORDER BY p.name;

FROM project_mapping pm
JOIN repos r ON r.id = pm.row_id
WHERE pm.`table` = 'repos'
  AND pm.project_name IN (SELECT upm_g.project_name FROM user_project_mapping upm_g WHERE upm_g.user_login = ${__user.login:sqlstring} AND upm_g.project_name IN ($project))

list.definition:
-- GitHub authors of merged PRs in the selected projects, repositories and time range: the table
-- matches PRs on the author's GitHub account, so other people could never match a row.
WITH pr_authors AS (
  SELECT CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(pr.author_id, ':', -1) AS UNSIGNED) AS gid, MAX(pr.author_name) AS login
  FROM pull_requests pr
  WHERE pr.base_repo_id IN (SELECT pm.row_id FROM project_mapping pm WHERE pm.`table` = 'repos' AND pm.project_name IN (SELECT upm_g.project_name FROM user_project_mapping upm_g WHERE upm_g.user_login = ${__user.login:sqlstring} AND upm_g.project_name IN ($project)))
    AND ('__all' IN ($repo_id) OR pr.base_repo_id IN ($repo_id))
    AND pr.status = 'MERGED' AND $__timeFilter(pr.merged_date)
    AND pr.author_id LIKE 'github:GithubAccount:%' AND pr.author_name NOT LIKE '%[bot]'
  GROUP BY 1
),
named AS (
  -- Account 0 is GitHub's placeholder for deleted users.
  SELECT a.gid, COALESCE(ga.login, NULLIF(a.login, ''), 'Unknown user') AS handle,
    COALESCE(NULLIF(ga.name, ''), ga.login, NULLIF(a.login, ''), 'Unknown user') AS name
  FROM pr_authors a
  LEFT JOIN (SELECT id, MAX(login) AS login, MAX(name) AS name FROM _tool_github_accounts GROUP BY id) ga ON ga.id = a.gid
)
-- The GitHub handle is added when two people share a name.
SELECT CONCAT(name, CASE WHEN COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY name) > 1 AND handle <> name THEN CONCAT(' (', handle, ')') ELSE '' END) AS __text,
  CONCAT('gh:', gid) AS __value
FROM named
ORDER BY __text;
